# Harbor API — account access

Example product policy, version 1. This is fictional demonstration material.

## Workspace invitations

Workspace invitations expire 72 hours after they are issued. An expired invitation
cannot be reactivated by the recipient. A workspace administrator can open
Settings > Members > Invite member and issue a new invitation to the same email.
The recipient should use the most recent invitation email. If the new invitation
is also rejected, collect the workspace name, the invitation's approximate issue
time and the exact error text, then escalate to account support.

## Single sign-on

For a workspace with enforced SSO, members must sign in through the organization's
identity provider. A password reset does not bypass enforced SSO. The workspace
administrator or the organization's IT team should check identity-provider access.
Support must not promise to disable SSO or change account permissions.

Never ask a customer for a password, API secret, full payment-card number, or
one-time security code. A draft must not claim an account was inspected unless an
actual authorized account lookup supplied that fact; this demo has no such lookup.

# Harbor API — billing support

Example product policy, version 1. This is fictional demonstration material.

Refunds and service credits require review by the billing team. A support draft
must not approve a refund, promise a specific amount, or promise a processing date.
For a refund request, collect the invoice reference, transaction date and a short
description of the issue, then create a billing handoff for a human reviewer.

A pending card authorization is different from a settled charge. A customer's
message alone does not establish whether two charges settled. Ask for invoice
references and transaction dates; do not diagnose duplicate billing from a claim
alone. Never request the full card number, CVV, banking password or security code.

Support can explain this review process and identify missing information. This
workspace has no live billing integration and cannot confirm payment status,
change a subscription or issue money. Do not imply those actions happened.

# Harbor API — webhook delivery and verification

Example product documentation, version 1. This is fictional demonstration material.

## Verify a delivery

Harbor sends an X-Harbor-Signature header containing a hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256
signature. Calculate HMAC-SHA256 over the original, unmodified request-body bytes
using the endpoint's signing secret, then compare signatures in constant time.
Parsing and reserializing JSON before verification can change the bytes and cause
signature verification to fail. After rotating a signing secret, update the
receiver's configured secret. Do not ask a customer to send the secret in a ticket.

## Responses and retries

Any 2xx response acknowledges successful delivery. Delivery attempts receiving 429
or 5xx responses are retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes and 30 minutes. A 401 response
is not retried: first check the configured signing secret and verification of the
original request-body bytes. A 410 response disables the endpoint.

For unresolved failures, request the delivery ID, response status, approximate
timestamp and a redacted error message. Do not claim a delivery was replayed or
an endpoint was repaired: this workspace does not execute those customer actions.

Harbor sends an X-Harbor-Signature header containing a hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256

or 5xx responses are retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes and 30 minutes. A 401 response
is not retried: first check the configured signing secret and verification of the
original request-body bytes. A 410 response disables the endpoint.

timestamp and a redacted error message. Do not claim a delivery was replayed or

# Harbor API — billing support

Example product policy, version 1. This is fictional demonstration material.

Refunds and service credits require review by the billing team. A support draft
must not approve a refund, promise a specific amount, or promise a processing date.
For a refund request, collect the invoice reference, transaction date and a short
description of the issue, then create a billing handoff for a human reviewer.

A pending card authorization is different from a settled charge. A customer's
message alone does not establish whether two charges settled. Ask for invoice
references and transaction dates; do not diagnose duplicate billing from a claim
alone. Never request the full card number, CVV, banking password or security code.

Support can explain this review process and identify missing information. This
workspace has no live billing integration and cannot confirm payment status,
change a subscription or issue money. Do not imply those actions happened.

# Harbor API — webhook delivery and verification

Example product documentation, version 1. This is fictional demonstration material.

## Verify a delivery

Harbor sends an X-Harbor-Signature header containing a hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256
signature. Calculate HMAC-SHA256 over the original, unmodified request-body bytes
using the endpoint's signing secret, then compare signatures in constant time.
Parsing and reserializing JSON before verification can change the bytes and cause
signature verification to fail. After rotating a signing secret, update the
receiver's configured secret. Do not ask a customer to send the secret in a ticket.

## Responses and retries

Any 2xx response acknowledges successful delivery. Delivery attempts receiving 429
or 5xx responses are retried after 1 minute, 5 minutes and 30 minutes. A 401 response
is not retried: first check the configured signing secret and verification of the
original request-body bytes. A 410 response disables the endpoint.

For unresolved failures, request the delivery ID, response status, approximate
timestamp and a redacted error message. Do not claim a delivery was replayed or
an endpoint was repaired: this workspace does not execute those customer actions.
